import numpy as np
P=np.array([[0.25,0.75],[0.75,0.25]])
nu=np.array([0.5,0.5]); xi=nu@P; m=nu+xi
Q=np.diag(1/m)@(np.diag(nu)@P+P.T@np.diag(nu))
pi=m/m.sum(); delta=np.array([1.,-1.])
K_paper=Q@np.diag(1/m)
K_correct=Q@np.diag(1/pi)@Q.T
print('Aperiodic, irreducible example, t=1:')
print('P_nu =',Q.tolist())
print('Equation (7) eigenvalues:',np.linalg.eigvalsh(K_paper).tolist())
print('Equation (6) claimed squared distance:',float(delta@K_paper@delta))
print('Defined diffusion distance squared:',float(delta@K_correct@delta))
print('Correct kernel equals Z P_nu"'^(2t) D_m''^(-1):'"',np.allclose(K_correct,m.sum()*np.linalg.matrix_power(Q,2)@np.diag(1/m)))
W=np.array([[1.,2.,0.],[2.,1.,1.],[0.,1.,1.]])
Q=W/W.sum(axis=1,keepdims=True)
m=W.sum(axis=1); pi=m/m.sum()
K_gram=Q@np.diag(1/pi)@Q.T
v=np.array([1.,-1.,0.])
print('Irregular-degree example, correct Gram distance:',float(v@K_gram@v))
print('Distance from using its rows as Euclidean features:',float(v@K_gram@K_gram.T@v))
for label, vals in [
 ('Table 1 proposed', [90.11,44.39,86.50,73.90,87.49,36.08,62.40,60.43,78.95,72.19,34.05]),
 ('Table 4 proposed', [90.11,42.13,84.73,70.24,83.19,36.08,59.34,54.90,74.89,68.79,33.60]),
 ('Table 4 DSC+', [68.63,36.58,91.09,61.12,79.45,22.97,54.24,51.64,74.80,31.46,27.47])
]: print(label,'mean',round(sum(vals)/len(vals),3))
PY"

strengths: Significance: Clustering sparse directed graphs that are not strongly connected is a useful problem. The proposed combination of vertex reweighting and diffusion offers a flexible approach, and Figure 1 illustrates its potential for recovering structure at different scales.

Originality: Combining generalized graph Laplacians, diffusion filtering, and CH/DCH parameter selection is a coherent methodological contribution. Under appropriate assumptions, the parametrized operator has a valid interpretation as a reversible walk on reweighted, symmetrized flows.

Evidence: The experiments cover 11 UCI datasets and four networks. Particularly valuable are the appendix experiments using CH/DCH instead of labels for parameter selection: the reduced-parameter variant reports average UCI NMI of 63.45 versus 60.01 for PIC, and substantial improvements on Cora.

Presentation and ethics: The high-level progression and algorithm descriptions are accessible, and dataset sources, sizes, and parameter grids are supplied. No material research-ethics concern is evident from the described public-benchmark experiments.
weaknesses: Soundness: The central diffusion-distance identity is incorrect as written. With m=ν+ξ and Z=sum(m), its Gram matrix is Pν^t Dπν^(-1)(Pν^t)^T = Z Pν^(2t) Dm^(-1), whereas Eq. (7) uses Pν^t Dm^(-1). This can be indefinite: for Pν=[[1/4,3/4],[3/4,1/4]], ν=(1/2,1/2), and t=1, the proposed quadratic form produces a squared distance of -1. Furthermore, Algorithm 1 clusters kernel rows as Euclidean features, inducing KK^T rather than K. Correcting the displayed identity alone would therefore not establish the algorithm's claimed diffusion geometry.

Soundness and scope: Self-adjointness and aperiodicity do not establish the ergodicity asserted in Section 3. The operator remains reducible when the underlying undirected support is disconnected. The formulas also require conventions for zero in/out-degrees and strictly positive vertex measures; the proposed measure can contain zeros. These missing assumptions undermine the claim of applicability to arbitrary digraphs.

Evaluation: Section 6.1 selects parameters using ground-truth agreement without describing a held-out validation protocol. Although baselines also receive label-based tuning, the proposed method searches 11×11×101 parameter combinations, substantially more than competitors. Best-of-100 restart results lack uncertainty estimates and a clear restart-selection criterion. The appendix's unsupervised results partially address this concern, but evaluate a reduced-parameter variant; they do not establish reliable unsupervised tuning of the full method or validate transferring Algorithm 2's diffusion time from a uniform measure to a tuned measure.

Originality and attribution: The operator directly inherits the generalized Laplacian of Sevi et al. (2022), yet the evaluation omits generalized spectral clustering using the same vertex measure. Consequently, the benefit of diffusion filtering is not isolated. Directionality claims also need matched ablations: the Cora winner uses α=0 with Eq. (12), which reduces to a walk on W+W^T, so that prominent gain does not demonstrate a benefit from retaining edge orientation.

Reproducibility and technical presentation: The manuscript provides no code link and leaves feature preprocessing insufficiently specified. Reported RSC settings such as τ=0.2 and 2.9 contradict the stated integer search grid. Appendix Eq. (12) also changes the operator's stationary weights to the modified measure plus ξ without specifying the corresponding kernel normalization. These ambiguities obstruct faithful reproduction.

Significance and limitations: Computational efficiency is not established. Matrix powers generally become dense, Algorithm 1 uses N-dimensional embeddings for N vertices, and the parameter search is substantial, yet no runtime, memory, or scaling measurements are supplied; the largest evaluated graph has 2,485 vertices. The limitations discussion should explicitly delimit these costs, connectivity requirements, and reliance on a supplied cluster count. Together with the central mathematical and evaluation gaps, these issues prevent acceptance despite the promising empirical results.
